verdict.rationale: The skills ship SKILL.md descriptions phrased around task context (e.g. 'before planning or implementing a requested change'), use user-intent-first naming, and include a validator that checks invocation contracts, which suggests deliberately designed activation. Nothing explicitly documents that installed skills trigger automatically from task context, and any auto-activation would come from the host agent rather than from YYLO itself. missing for 10: explicit documentation of automatic context-based triggering, a stated description/trigger-engineering guideline, hands-on evidence that agents activate the right skill at the right moment.

support.subject: As a developer, installed skills trigger automatically from task context, with descriptions engineered so the agent activates the right skill at the right moment

citations.quote: Inspect the current product architecture, dependencies, and validation loops before planning or implementing a requested change.
It checks nested references for retired lifecycle instructions as well as invocation contracts and plugin version parity.
